solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Moving up with risk — mountaineer's sling is the answer

indicators.note: something moving shifts position, so the letters that follow are shifted into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two words of fodder

explanation.surface: Climbing is dangerous, so a climber's safety sling is the solution to the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A Prusik is a loop of cord tied to a rope with a friction knot, used by climbers to ascend or as a safety backup.

clue.text: Suffering comes to nimble mover? One may go the wall

parts.note: suffering is pain
to troll is, in Chambers, to move nimbly or roll about, so one who does is a troller

explanation.surface: Someone in agony arrives at a sprightly dancer, perhaps on the way to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a decorator's tool is pushed up and down a wall, and the phrase plays on 'go to the wall', meaning to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator's cylindrical brush applies emulsion across interior plaster surfaces, so it literally travels over the wall.

clue.text: Sort of webbed article carried by two friends

indicators.note: what is carried is held between the bearers, so one piece sits inside the pair

parts.note: two words for a friend, pal and mate, side by side
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is delivered by a couple of mates.
explanation.walkthrough: The article sits between the two friends. 'Sort of' is fair because the word is a rarer form meaning web-footed.
explanation.definitionFit: Palamate is a zoological term describing feet joined by membranes between the toes, as in ducks.

clue.text: One adequate factory closed off plant

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a closed-off section is shut away and no longer counted, so that part of the word is dropped

parts.note: adequate means satisfactory
the word itself, which is the part removed

explanation.surface: A single passable works has been shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own word 'factory' is the chunk removed from the end of satisfactory, leaving I SATIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatis is the botanical genus of woad, a flowering herb once grown for blue dye.

clue.text: Plant in square opened by Her Majesty

indicators.note: a thing opened up has something entering its middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A garden in a town square is opened by the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerine is a genus of South African bulbs with bright lily-like flowers, including the Guernsey lily.

clue.text: Rascally old soldiers upset fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset thing is turned upside down, so the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
a guy is a fellow

explanation.surface: Veteran troops of bad character overturned a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguy is an obsolete adjective formed from rogue, meaning knavish or behaving like a scoundrel.

clue.text: Each pig south of lake in pasture

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
EA is the abbreviation for each
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Every pig grazes in a meadow below the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of lake' places the lake first in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasow is a dialect and old word for grazing land, related to lea, a grassy field.

clue.text: See farm animal, with river rising, in plant that makes it mad?

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
a cow is a farm animal

indicators.note: in a down answer something rising goes upward, so the river's name is read from the bottom

parts.note: the Dee is a British river

explanation.surface: Cattle by a rising river eat a weed that sends them crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is playful: loco is Spanish for mad, and the plant poisons livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Locoweed is a North American legume that causes neurological illness in grazing livestock, making them behave erratically.

clue.text: Free advice no longer given to them

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for advice, hence 'no longer'
'em, the casual short form of them

explanation.surface: People who no longer get advice are set at liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a captive or pawned item is to release it by paying, which sets it at liberty.

clue.text: Stand up outside a cairn

indicators.note: one word lying outside another wraps round it, so the short piece goes within

parts.note: to stand up is to rise
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get to their feet beside a pile of stones on a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots and northern dialect a raise is a heap of stones built as a memorial or landmark on high ground.

clue.text: Communication from Paris about to be taken to north European

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A message from the French capital concerns someone from the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From Paris' asks for a French word; the order follows 'about' being attached after the Latvian.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettre is the French noun for a letter, a written message sent by post.

clue.text: Like intimate combat that you've just seen here!

definitions.meaning: surface reading: describing a fight between just two people, man to man
setter's reading: the clue's own number, printed as two ones, is what you read just before the clue

explanation.surface: Describing a private duel, the kind of thing you've just witnessed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue number 11 is read digit by digit, and that same pair of words describes a one-to-one fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives this hyphenated form as meaning one-to-one, a contest or meeting between two individuals alone.

clue.text: Part of body giving neural disorder

indicators.note: disorder means things are out of their proper sequence, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A limb is showing signs of a nervous illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulnare is a small wrist bone on the ulna side of the carpus, so it is an anatomical piece.

clue.text: Darling daughter marked with favour?

parts.note: Grace Darling, the lighthouse keeper's daughter who rescued shipwrecked sailors in 1838
D abbreviates daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A beloved daughter was singled out for special kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like an endearment, but it is a surname: Grace Darling is a famous English heroine of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be graced is to be honoured or adorned, which means being shown approval or kindness by someone.

clue.text: Female energy with which Indian widow ensnares king

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap something so it is held inside, so one piece is caught within another

parts.note: sati is a Hindu widow who immolated herself on her husband's pyre
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A woman's vigour is what lets a bereaved Indian wife capture a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism Sakti (Shakti) is the divine feminine power, the energy of a god personified as his consort.

clue.text: American head of society appears in ripped silk

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the pair go within the next word

parts.note: ripped is tore, past tense of tear
US is short for American

indicators.note: the head of something is its front end, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of society

explanation.surface: A US society hostess turns up wearing a torn silk gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse brownish silk produced by wild Indian silkworms, also spelt tussah or tussar.

clue.text: Capture man with bad habit, fellow with wicked wife

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the word next to it comes out muddled

parts.note: taken as written
in Genesis Lot's wife looked back at sinful Sodom and was turned to a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: Someone arrests a man with a nasty vice and a fellow with a bad wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capture man' is backgammon jargon, not policing: a blot is a lone piece open to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: In backgammon, to take an exposed single piece of the opponent is the phrase used for knocking it off the board.

clue.text: Women seen in foreign city station once

indicators.note: being seen within a place means standing inside it, so one letter is placed inside

parts.note: Rome is a city abroad
W abbreviates women

explanation.surface: Female travellers turn up at a railway terminus abroad in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' means a place or position, not a railway stop; 'once' marks the Spenserian spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowme is an old spelling of room in its sense of a place or position someone occupies.

clue.text: Heathen god with imposing bearing, one to spoil the fun of old

definitions.text: one to spoil the fun of old

parts.note: Mars, Roman god of war
port is a stately carriage or deportment

explanation.surface: A pagan deity of stately manner is a killjoy from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsport is an obsolete term for a spoilsport, someone who wrecks the enjoyment of others.

clue.text: Genius is leading Ireland, high-ranking woman

parts.note: in Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spirit or genius
taken as written
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A brilliant mind is running Ireland, and she is a top lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Genius here is a guardian spirit, not a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kaiserin is a German empress, the wife of a Kaiser or a woman reigning in her own right.

clue.text: He is naughty nabbing two maidens put in a trap

indicators.note: to nab is to grab and hold, so the shuffled letters take the pair inside
a naughty child will not behave, so these letters will not stay in line

parts.note: taken as written
M is a maiden over in cricket scoring, so two make MM

explanation.surface: A mischievous man grabbing two young women ensnares them.
explanation.definitionFit: Immesh is a variant of enmesh, to catch in a net or tangle as in a snare.

clue.text: Quiet old character died, reduced to a minimum?

parts.note: p, piano, is quiet in music
a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet
d. is short for died

explanation.surface: A quiet elderly eccentric has died, cut down to almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' suggests a person but means a letter of an ancient script.
explanation.definitionFit: Pruned means cut back, trimmed hard; the question mark admits that pruning need not go all the way down.

clue.text: Marched — and walked in step periodically

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the past tense goes between the kept letters
something done periodically happens at intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first and third letters of step
trod is the past tense of tread, to walk

explanation.surface: Soldiers paraded, keeping in time now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Strode is the past tense of stride, to walk with long purposeful steps, as marching soldiers do.

clue.text: House-to-house transporters bring me back into Bristol team?

indicators.note: putting something into another places it inside, so the turned word goes within the team

parts.note: Bristol Rovers is a professional English football club

indicators.note: going back means reading the short word from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A football fan asks to be restored to the Bristol side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House-to-house' means moving from one home to another, not door-to-door selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Removers, in British usage, are a firm that carries furniture and belongings when people relocate homes.

clue.text: Poet or knight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the legendary Gaelic bard whose epics Macpherson claimed to translate
second meaning: the same figure as a warrior of the Fianna, Finn's band of heroes

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses point to one legendary Irish figure, Oisín, who was both bard and warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gaelic legend Oisín, son of Finn, was both the reciter of heroic songs and a fighting member of Finn's company.

clue.text: Drug — the classical way to swallow a grain

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the next pieces go within the Latin word

parts.note: via is Latin for road or way
taken as written
gr is the abbreviation for grain, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Medicine instructions: the ancient route is to swallow a small grain of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Viagra is the brand name of sildenafil, a prescription medicine for erectile dysfunction.

clue.text: Gentleman admitting love before end of the party

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so the round letter goes inside

parts.note: sire, an old respectful term for a man of rank
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the

explanation.surface: A gentleman confesses his love just before the party winds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A soirée is an evening gathering held in a private house, usually with conversation or music.

clue.text: Wild tree hiding a plant

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the single letter goes within
wild things are untamed and disordered, so the letters of the word beside it run loose

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An untamed tree conceals a smaller plant beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reate is an old name for water crowfoot, an aquatic buttercup that grows in streams.

clue.text: Rascal in danger, half hidden on top of tree

indicators.note: with half of it hidden, only the other half of the word stays in view

parts.note: danger is risk
an elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A scamp in peril is partly concealed at the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of the danger word is hidden; 'on top of' sets the rest above the tree in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Skelm is a Scots and South African word for a scoundrel or rogue, from Dutch.

clue.text: Big organisation in financial trouble or still in good order as before?

definitions.text: still in good order as before?

parts.note: UN, the United Nations
broke means having no money

explanation.surface: A huge body is in money difficulty, or perhaps still intact after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks the archaic form of unbroken.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbroke is an old form of unbroken, meaning intact and undamaged, still in sound condition.

clue.text: Greek character maybe wanting lobsters, not cold

indicators.note: 'not' a given letter tells the solver that letter is left out

parts.note: scampi are Norway lobsters, hence 'maybe'
C stands for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A fussy Greek diner might want shellfish, but not served chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampi is an obsolete letter of the Greek alphabet, later used only as the numeral for 900.

clue.text: In night of informality, see someone by river

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the short word goes within the informal spelling

parts.note: nite is the casual spelling of night
lo is an old word for look or see

explanation.surface: On a relaxed evening out, you spot someone beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The river is the Nile; the definition is cryptically vague.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nilote is a member of a group of peoples living in the upper Nile valley of East Africa.

clue.text: Title, something conveying meaning to the rank and file

parts.note: a sign is something that conveys meaning
OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An honorific: some gesture that conveys a message to the ordinary troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Signor is the Italian courtesy title equivalent to Mr, used before a man's name.

clue.text: Boy, one knocked over, showing no lumps?

indicators.note: a thing knocked over ends up the other way round, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad has been knocked flat, and he has no bruises to show.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: lumps stands for nodes, and a botanical stem without nodes is described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Enodal means without nodes, the knots or joints along a stem, so smooth and free of swellings.

clue.text: Top female taking time, getting about — behind as before?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the queen at the top
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A leading lady takes her time going round and ends up at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Arere is an obsolete adverb meaning backward or in the rear, so a word for behind used in older English.

clue.text: Depression, with restricted period at home a decisive factor

indicators.note: a hollow holding things with it encloses them, so the following pieces go inside

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
a term is a fixed, limited period
in means at home
taken as written

explanation.surface: Low mood, with a spell confined indoors, proves the deciding element.
explanation.definitionFit: A determinant is anything that settles or strongly shapes an outcome, a controlling cause.
